blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) warned the public against gathering, selling and consuming shellfish from four coastal areas in Eastern Visayas. The alert comes after laboratory tests detected paralytic shellfish toxins associated with red tide. In its advisory dated Nov. 12, BFAR-8 identified Carigara Bay, Irong-Irong Bay, Matarinao Bay and Cambatutay Bay as areas where shellfish samples tested positive for red tide toxins. Carigara Bay spans across the coasts of Babatngon, San Miguel, Capoocan, Barugo and Carigara towns in Leyte and Irong-Irong Bay in Catbalogan City, Samar.
